To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) 2D and especially 3D bounding-boxes are insufficient representations of objects and that 2) a 3D representation of objects that allows reasoning on the fine detail-level of 3D shapes is beneficial.
(1) jointly modeling the 3D shapes of multiple objects leads to better scene interpretations and (2) this is particularly true for objects that are close to each other.
(i) the 3D shapes of multiple objects in street scenes are highly correlated and (ii) the 3-dimensional shapes of multiple objects can be jointly estimated from a set of 2-dimensional images.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following question: can we improve the state-of-the-art in scene understanding by moving away from bounding boxes and towards 3D shape representations of objects?

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we are able to jointly estimate the 3D wireframes of cars in a scene, while taking into account the occlusion between them, and we show that this leads to more accurate 3D shape estimates of the individual objects.
we show that it is possible to jointly estimate the 3D geometry of objects in a scene and their 3D relative pose, in a way that is robust to partial visibility and occlusions.
we are able to estimate the 3D shapes of objects in a street scene, while also estimating the 3d shape of the road surface.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the 3D shapes of objects can be jointly estimated in a scene, and that this representation allows to express object-object interactions on a much more detailed level.

, in order to achieve robust scene understanding, we need to move away from the current coarse representations, and design representations that can express the 3D geometry of individual objects on a fine detail level, and that can reason jointly about the geometry of multiple objects.
3D shape estimation can be achieved with a simple and robust approach, and that this approach is more effective than the state-of-the-art methods that rely on complex and fragile reasoning schemes.
